meaning:
θανατόω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for מוּת hi., ho., also for הָרַג, etc. ;]
to put to death: with accusative, Mat.10:21 26:59 27:1, Mrk.13:12 14:55, Luk.21:16, 2Co.6:9, 1Pe.3:18; pass., Rom.8:36. Metaphorical: Rom.8:13; pass., with dative, (in relation to), Rom.7:4.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.
“Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.
You will be handed over even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. They will cause some of you to be put to death.
Therefore, my brothers, you also were made dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you would be joined to another, to him who was raised from the…
as unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and behold, we live; as punished, and not killed;
Because Christ also suffered for sins once, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring you to God, being put to death in the flesh, but made alive…
